maria: Heads-up — running through the Go SDK sampleapp onboarding and I can repro a goroutine leak when cancelling a generator stream mid-flight.

sam: ugh, seen this. is the leak related to auth refresh blocking the stream handshake?

maria: I think so. sampleapp's token refresh is synchronous inside the stream loop. snippet: 
```
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() {
  if shouldRefreshToken() { refreshBlocking() }
  // process token chunks
}
```
If ctx is cancelled while refreshBlocking() is running the generator never returns.

dev-bot: CI: stream-cancel-test failed 3x on main with goroutine count spike — https://ci.internal/redwood/stream-cancel

gina: (typo, meant ina) Quick thought: move refresh into a goroutine and select on ctx.Done() inside provider. That avoids blocking the response loop.

ina: Confirming — non-blocking token provider + context-aware refresh prevents the hang. Also ensure generator iterator Close()/Cancel() actually signals underlying HTTP/client.

raj: I'll draft a small change to sampleapp replacing blocking refresh with a context-aware provider and add a test that cancels after N tokens and asserts goroutine count stability.

olivia: +1. Also let's add a short section in the Go quickstart about "stream cancellation and auth callbacks" — JS already has this pattern.

sam: For SDK parity: JS/py have token-provider examples that avoid blocking. We should port that to Go and make it a first-class helper in the SDK (TokenProviderWithContext or similar).

maria: Filing an issue now with repro steps and heap/goroutine snapshots. Will link PR when ready.

ina: I can review the test and help craft the snapshot assertion. Would prefer a minimal integration test (local fake server) instead of full e2e.

raj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/789 — changes sampleapp, adds token provider helper and test.

olivia: :thumbsup: Nice. After merge we should update the streaming README and the onboarding quickstart so new users don't hit this.
